chapter: Boyhood in Webster Groves and early roadhouse work
title: Summer jobs and the trip to Lincoln
summary: With a buddy he mowed lawns and dug ditches to ease the family burden. His mother packed a week of food for the four-hour, 125-mile trip.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What other sort, you were talking about sort of working during the summer, of things would you have done in those days to raise money.
Well, Stan, we did, buddy and I mostly, we'd go out and look for work. We'd cut lawns.
I was going to say mow lawns.

We'd mow the lawns and that sort of thing and then we got game. We got real game and we went to dig some ditches because digging the ditches paid a whole lot of money, you know. And, at 12 o'clock ... through.

Oh, yeah, yeah. And we wanted to do something to take that weight off of our families.

It is. It's a tremendous expense and on the way to that trip my mother packed me enough food to last a week. And she was right because the food was ridiculous. Only had to go 125 miles, took us four hours.
